## In this session

-   **What is scholarly editing?**
-   Discussion of [@sahle2017]
-   **TEI**: the Text Encoding Initiative as a data model for text

## What is scholarly editing?

-   The edition as a *representation* of a work, not a copy of it
-   Diplomatic, critical, genetic, documentary — what each foregrounds
-   Sahle's wheel: text as document, as visual object, as linguistic sign, as work, as version
-   What "digital" changes: not the medium, but what the edition can be *for*

## TEI

-   TEI as a customisable XML vocabulary and as a community
-   The header: an edition's metadata is part of the edition
-   Core encoding: structure, persons, places, dates, editorial intervention
-   `<choice>`, `<orig>`, `<reg>`, `<del>`, `<add>` — encoding uncertainty and change
-   Customisation with ODD, and why every project ends up with its own subset

## Connecting back

Look at the models you built in [Session 4](/contents/sessions/04.qmd). TEI is a data model too
— it just happens to be embedded in the text rather than held alongside it. What does that
placement make easy, and what does it make hard?

::: {.callout-tip title="In parallel in the Lab"}
The [DH Lab](https://dhbern.github.io/dh-lab/contents/sessions/07.html) does TEI hands-on the
same week, as a form of data publication.
:::
